hero: In the emergency room of a provincial hospital in Bohol, a young Filipino resident holds a drained, cloudy peritoneal dialysis bag in front of a printed page while a Filipino nephrology fellow gently examines the catheter exit site on the abdomen of a weathered middle-aged fisherman lying on a stretcher, his wife beside him holding a bag of supplies; early morning light, urgent but calm, no text in image.

figures.teaches: PD peritonitis is diagnosed by two of three criteria, treated within an hour, and judged by the daily effluent count with a fixed decision day.
figures.content: Top band 'Diagnosis (ISPD 2022, 1C): at least 2 of 3' with three icons: (1) 'Pain and/or cloudy effluent', (2) 'Effluent WBC >100/µL after a dwell of at least 2 h, with >50% neutrophils', (3) 'Positive culture'. Middle band 'The first hour': Keep the bag -> Examine (abdomen, exit site, tunnel) -> Send cell count, Gram stain, culture in blood culture bottles BEFORE antibiotics (1C) -> Start unit protocol: IP antibiotics covering gram-positive and gram-negative (1C; IP route 1B) + antifungal prophylaxis (1B) -> Look for surgical abdomen. Bottom band: line graph 'Effluent WBC by day' (days 1-7) with a falling green curve labeled 'responding' and a flat red curve labeled 'refractory'; vertical marker at day 5 'Decision day: not clear after 5 days = remove catheter (1D); clearly falling = may observe longer (2C)'. Side box 'Remove the catheter': refractory (1D), fungal (1C, immediate), relapsing/recurrent/repeat (consider, 1C), exit or tunnel infection with peritonitis by the same bacterium (2C). Footer '© renalcarematters.com'.

figures.teaches: Catheter infections travel inward from the exit site, and dialysate leaks travel outward to the weakest point.
figures.content: Sagittal cutaway of the lower abdomen: PD catheter from a lateral exit site through the subcutaneous tunnel with superficial and deep cuffs, entering the peritoneum, coiled tip in the pelvis. Numbered labels with clue boxes: 1 'Exit-site infection: pus with or without redness (ISPD 2023)'; 2 'Tunnel infection: tenderness, swelling, induration along the tunnel; ultrasound may help'; 3 'Pericatheter leak: wet dressing'; 4 'Abdominal wall / genital leak: swelling of wall, scrotum or labia'; 5 'Hernia: bulge at umbilicus, groin or incision'; 6 'Pleuroperitoneal leak: right effusion high in glucose, stop PD'; 7 'Tip migration out of pelvis: positional drainage'; 8 'Constipation: bowel compresses catheter, slow outflow, treat first'. Red arrows inward from exit to peritoneum labeled 'Infection route'; blue arrows outward labeled 'Fluid escapes'. Footer '© renalcarematters.com'.
